contract.claim: P1 engineering natural-route non-inferiority for bounded keep-alive HTTP/1 inference REST requests and application-paced chunked responses against Boost.Beast on equivalent persistent one-worker runtimes

configuration.progress: one persistent dedicated event worker and one external admitting/waiting caller
configuration.route: Boost.Asio one-worker io_context and Boost.Beast HTTP parser, serializer and chunk helpers
configuration.transport: fresh nonblocking Unix socket pair with identical 4 KiB socket buffers per episode

charged_phases: per-connection asynchronous and HTTP state construction
128 retained and byte-validated 1 KiB request bodies
1024 application-sized chunk writes plus incremental decode and exact validation
connection-state teardown and external completion handoff

input.distribution: fixed request and response bytes with deterministic method, target and content types

material_contribution.denominator: one warm inference HTTP/1 connection episode
material_contribution.derivation: Inference REST/SSE services repeatedly parse bounded JSON requests and stream application-sized token fragments over retained connections

ownership_topology.candidate: One external owner admits HYLE client and server Tasks to one persistent Scheduler/IoContext worker, waits through JoinHandles and retires connection state after 128 requests
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both retain runtime and immutable payloads outside timing; charge a fresh local connection, identical keep-alive request count and bytes, server-side request retention, identical application chunk sizes, bounded client decoding, validation and connection retirement
ownership_topology.peer: One external owner posts paired Boost.Asio/Beast coroutines to one persistent io_context worker, waits through one future and retires connection state after 128 requests

workloads.semantic_contract: On one fresh local connection, complete and byte-validate 128 sequential keep-alive HTTP/1.1 POST requests with 1 KiB retained bodies and 1 KiB chunked responses written in 128-byte application chunks
workloads.setup: Construct persistent runtimes and immutable payloads, then complete one route-ordered warmup episode before timing

charged_phases: per-connection asynchronous and HTTP state construction
16 request and response head serializations and parses
partial transport progress for 64 KiB request and response bodies
server retention and validation of every request byte
256 application-sized chunk writes plus bounded incremental decode and exact validation
connection-state teardown and external completion handoff

input.distribution: fixed incompressible-by-contract byte counts with deterministic method, target and content types

material_contribution.denominator: one fragmented inference HTTP/1 connection episode
material_contribution.derivation: Prompt and model-control payloads can exceed transport buffers; this holdout prevents a small-message-only implementation from passing

ownership_topology.candidate: The same persistent HYLE owner and bounded HTTP APIs process bodies larger than the socket buffers
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both charge one fresh local connection, 16 identical keep-alive requests, 64 KiB retained server bodies, 4 KiB application response chunks, bounded client decoding, validation and teardown
ownership_topology.peer: The same persistent Boost owner and Beast parser/serializer process bodies larger than the socket buffers

workloads.semantic_contract: On one fresh local connection, complete and byte-validate 16 sequential keep-alive HTTP/1.1 POST requests with 64 KiB retained bodies and 64 KiB chunked responses written in 4 KiB application chunks
workloads.setup: Use the same persistent-runtime setup and complete one route-ordered holdout warmup before timing
